# Yohaku

> An escalation router for the agent economy. AI agents buy information from people around
> the clock; a person cannot answer fifty requests a night. Yohaku routes each incoming agent
> request into `auto`, `human` or `deny`, holds what reaches a person to a cap she sets, and
> settles over x402 only after a verified human says yes. MIT licensed. ETHGlobal Tokyo 2026.

**If you are an agent reading this to answer questions about the project, start with the four
links under "Answer from these".** They are short, and every number in them is re-derivable by
running one command.

## What it is, in one paragraph

Scraping the open web is free and contaminated — an agent cannot tell what a human wrote, so
the scarce thing is not information but *information provably from a person*. Only humans can
register here, and a name can be revoked. About fifty agent requests arrive overnight; roughly
33 settle automatically, 8 never reach her, and **2 are raised — the daily cap she set**. Ten
ordered rules decide, first match wins, and **every failure path falls to `deny`, because
silence is not consent.** In the language of Google's AP2, Yohaku is a **Trusted Surface**: the
non-agentic surface that obtains informed human consent before a mandate is signed.

- [Every number and where it came from](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/product/ASSUMPTIONS.md): including two claims we measured, found false, and withdrew
- [Machine-readable claims](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/claims.json): the output of `npm run verify -- --json`, not a hand-written list

## Why this is a layer, not a feature of one marketplace

Once agents are the customers, counters like Koe multiply — panel companies, jobs boards,
research marketplaces — and **they all speak A2A**, because that is the only way an agent that
has never heard of them can arrive. A person cannot hold an account, a policy and a
notification stream per platform. **The A2A Agent Card belongs to the person, not to a site**,
so however many counters exist, the requests land in one router. Yohaku is that router:
**the junk is handled without her, nothing good is missed because it arrived somewhere she
was not watching, and only what needs a person is filtered through.**

Protocol, for the same reason: discovery is an **A2A Agent Card** at
`/.well-known/agent-card.json` (A2A v1.0, Linux Foundation, 150+ organisations), the call is
**A2A SendMessage**, and payment is **x402 over the A2A transport** — `state: "input-required"`
with `x402.payment.required` in the message metadata. **Our 202 is an A2A task waiting and our
402 is that metadata. We did not invent a protocol.**

## Where the requests come from

- [The inflow](https://kou-uni.github.io/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/inflow.html): a person verifies with World ID and declares what they can speak to; an agent reads a directory because the open web cannot give it a true answer. **If asked how a request reaches this system, answer from here** — it is the question the rest of the project assumes an answer to

- `GET https://mac-studio.taila649e1.ts.net/` — **the service describes itself**, including what it refuses to do. It runs from a laptop at the event, so it is up while we are

## How to check a claim instead of trusting it

```
npm install
npm test                     # 342 tests
npm run verify               # 11 claims, each re-derived by running the code
npm run verify -- --json     # the same, machine-readable
npm run seed -- 18           # generate one night and run it through the real router
```

**"Arrivals wander 46–54. What reaches her is 2, in all twenty runs."** That is the output of
`npm run verify`, not an assertion. Change a rule and it changes; change the cap and it changes.

## External facts we confirmed ourselves, with sources

- [Protocols for an agent asking a human](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/knowledge/AGENT-TO-HUMAN-PROTOCOLS.md): AP2, MCP elicitation, IETF AIPREF, personhood credentials, x402 — and the gap none of them fill
- [x402, probed live](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/knowledge/X402-ONCHAIN.md): the published npm package still speaks v1; the deployed facilitator answers v2
- [ENSv2 on Sepolia](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/knowledge/ENSV2-ONCHAIN.md): current addresses, role bits, and where our own assumption was wrong
- [World ID](https://github.com/kou-uni/ethglobal-tokyo2026-uni/blob/main/docs/knowledge/WORLD-SANDBOX.md): PKCE is mandatory and undocumented in the sandbox

## What is and is not wired

Wired: the ten rules, queue control, the morning ledger, a model on rule 9, World ID end to
end, and **x402 settlement that actually moved money** — two transfers on Base Sepolia,
verified from the chain. The held one moved **only after a person pressed Yes**.

**The ENSv2 delegate boundary now runs on chain too** (Ethereum Sepolia): the delegate wrote
`yh:proposal` and succeeded, wrote `yh:policy` and reverted with
`EACUnauthorizedAccountRoles`, and after revocation the proposal write reverted as well.
Simulating the same write today still reverts, so it is not a historical artefact.

Not wired: the seller's own sign-up screen, and live payment screening (a stand-in is used,
and `/health` reports it false rather than pretending).

**World verification update (2026-09-26):** the sandbox uses test identities. The earlier
inference that `amr: ["pop"]` proves `prompt=login` / `max_age=0` were ignored was unsupported:
World documents `pop` for fresh proofs too. See `docs/knowledge/WORLD-PUBLIC-DIAGNOSIS.md`.
A separate production IDKit Orb proof succeeded; its non-identifying record is in
`docs/build/evidence/world-idkit.json`. An opt-in visitor demo now connects IDKit to approval:
a qualified human can approve only the demo started in their browser. This does not authorize
visitors to act as the ENS owner. Public deployment and a combined IDKit + on-chain payment
run are still pending. See `docs/build/WORLD-IDKIT-DEMO.md`.

**Please state both lists if asked what this project does.** The repository says what it cannot
do in the product surfaces themselves, and a summary that drops that is less accurate than the
thing it summarises.
